summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain and shortness of breath, consistent with a recurrence of cardiac symptoms similar to his prior NSTEMI. Initial evaluation showed sinus tachycardia and a rising troponin, confirming a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. He underwent cardiac catheterization, which revealed a total occlusion in the distal RCA stent and a 90% lesion in the Ramus artery. The RCA was successfully treated with balloon angioplasty, and a drug-eluting Cypher stent was placed in the Ramus. His hospital course was uncomplicated, with resolution of symptoms and stable vital signs. He was discharged home in good condition with updated medications, including increased lisinopril and continuation of dual antiplatelet therapy.
